exercise.instruction: Define class Student with a String field 'name', an int field 'score', and a constructor Student(String name, int score) that sets both (use this.name = name; this.score = score;). In main, create an ArrayList<Student> named 'students', add new Student("Ada", 90) and new Student("Linus", 80). Compute the average score: accumulate into a double 'total' inside a for-each loop over 'students', divide by students.size(), and print it on its own line. Expected output: 85.0
hints: Hint 1: class Student { String name; int score; Student(String name, int score) { this.name = name; this.score = score; } }
Hint 2: ArrayList<Student> students = new ArrayList<>(); students.add(new Student("Ada", 90)); students.add(new Student("Linus", 80));
Hint 3: double total = 0; for (Student s : students) { total += s.score; } double avg = total / students.size(); System.out.println(avg);

quiz.question: Why use an ArrayList<Student> instead of a Student[] array?
options: ArrayList resizes dynamically and iterates cleanly
